project.name: Dipoorlet
project.description: An offline quantization tool for ONNX models supporting multiple activation calibration algorithms (Mse, Minmax, Hist), weight transformation techniques (BiasCorrection, WeightEqualization, Adaround, Brecq, Qdrop), and generates quantitative parameters for multiple platforms (TensorRT, SNPE, RV, ATLAS, STPU, TI, i.MX, MagicMind, QNN).

nodes.name: __main__.py
nodes.summary: CLI entry point for Dipoorlet quantization tool. Orchestrates the full quantization pipeline: tensor calibration, weight transformation, profiling, and deployment to target platforms (TensorRT, MagicMind, RV, Atlas, SNPE, TI, IMX).

nodes.name: forward_net.py
nodes.summary: Provides forward pass utilities for ONNX models including ActivationCache for caching intermediate activations, and functions for minmax/histogram/OCTAV-based tensor statistics collection during calibration.

nodes.name: platform_settings.py
nodes.summary: Defines quantization settings for multiple deployment platforms (TensorRT, STPU, MagicMind, RV, Atlas, SNPE, TI, IMX, QNN). Contains layer type lists, quantization parameters (bit_width, per_channel, symmetric), and node configurations.

nodes.name: profiling.py
nodes.summary: Implements quantization profiling to measure layer-wise and model-level cosine similarity between floating-point and quantized outputs. Supports multipass and transformer-specific profiling modes.

nodes.name: quantize.py
nodes.summary: Core quantization logic for inserting fake quantization nodes into ONNX graphs. Handles QuantizeLinear/DequantizeLinear node insertion, weight/input quantization, and graph topology management.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Dipoorlet is an offline quantization tool for ONNX models. It supports multiple calibration algorithms (MSE, MinMax, Histogram), weight transformation techniques (AdaRound, BRECQ, Bias Correction, Weight Equalization), and targets deployment platforms including TensorRT, QNN, MagicMind, RV, Atlas, SNPE, TI, and IMX.

tour.title: CLI Entry Point
tour.description: The quantization pipeline is invoked via `python -m dipoorlet` using torchrun. The entry point at `dipoorlet/__main__.py` orchestrates the full workflow: tensor calibration, weight transformation, profiling, and deployment to target platforms. It uses distributed training helpers (MPI/SLURM) for multi-GPU calibration.

tour.title: Tensor Calibration — Activation Algorithms
tour.description: Dipoorlet offers three activation calibration algorithms, selectable at runtime via a dispatcher pattern: MinMax (simplest), Histogram (histogram-based percentile), and MSE/OCTAV (minimizes mean-squared error). The dispatcher in `tensor_cali/basic_algorithm.py` routes to the selected algorithm implementation. Calibration collects statistics from forward passes over a calibration dataset.

tour.title: Forward Pass and Activation Statistics
tour.description: Before calibration can run, the tool needs to collect activation statistics from the model. `forward_net.py` provides the forward pass utilities including `ActivationCache` for caching intermediate tensors, and specialized collectors for minmax (`forward_get_minmax`), histogram (`forward_get_hist`), and OCTAV/MSE (`forward_net_octav`) statistics. Transformer-specific variants handle memory-efficient collection for large models.

tour.title: Core Quantization — Inserting Fake Quant Nodes
tour.description: Once calibration yields clip values (min/max ranges), `quantize.py` transforms the ONNX graph by inserting QuantizeLinear/DequantizeLinear nodes. The `quant_graph` function orchestrates graph-wide insertion, while `insert_fake_quant_node` handles per-node insertion for weights and inputs. The `ONNXGraph` class in `utils.py` manages all ONNX model manipulation including topology changes and serialization.

tour.title: Weight Transformation — SOTA Finetune Algorithms
tour.description: Beyond basic calibration, Dipoorlet implements advanced weight transformation techniques to improve quantization accuracy: AdaRound (learning-based rounding of weights), BRECQ (bias correction for quantized layers), SparseQuant (channel-level pruning with quantization), Weight Equalization (balancing weight ranges across layers), and BatchNorm updates. These SOTA algorithms correct quantization error that basic calibration cannot address.

tour.title: Quantization Profiling and Analysis
tour.description: Dipoorlet provides detailed quantitative analysis to identify accuracy bottlenecks. The profiling module measures layer-wise and model-level cosine similarity between floating-point and quantized outputs. It supports multipass profiling (for standard CNNs) and transformer-specific profiling (using ActivationCache for memory efficiency). Layer-wise profiling removes quantized layers individually to find the most quantization-sensitive layers.

tour.title: Deployment Platform Settings
tour.description: Different deployment platforms (TensorRT, STPU, MagicMind, RV, Atlas, SNPE, TI, IMX, QNN) have distinct quantization requirements. `platform_settings.py` defines per-platform configuration including which layer types to quantize, bit_width, per_channel vs per_layer granularity, and symmetric vs asymmetric quantization. The `deploy/` directory contains platform-specific deployment logic.

tour.title: Platform-Specific Deployment Modules
tour.description: Each target hardware platform has its own deployment module: TensorRT (`deploy_trt.py`), QNN (`deploy_qnn.py`), MagicMind (`deploy_magicmind.py`), RV (`deploy_rv.py`), Atlas (`deploy_atlas.py`), SNPE (`deploy_snpe.py`), STPU (`deploy_stpu.py`), TI (`deploy_ti.py`), and IMX (`deploy_imx.py`). These modules adapt the quantized model output to each platform's required format and quantization parameters.

tour.title: Utilities — Logging, Data, and Distributed Support
tour.description: Supporting infrastructure includes: logging setup (`setup_logger`), clip value save/load for reusing calibration results, profiling result aggregation, input data generation for calibration batches, and distributed GPU coordination for multi-GPU calibration. The `dipoorlet_utils` module provides calibration utilities including TensorRT entropy calibrator and ImageNet/TinyImageNet dataset loaders.

tour.title: Demo Labs — End-to-End Workflows
tour.description: The DemoLab directory contains complete end-to-end examples: MobileNetV2 quantization with all calibration algorithms targeting TensorRT; ResNet18 quantization targeting both TensorRT and QNN (Qualcomm Neural Network); YOLOv8 quantization; and BEV object detection model quantization. Each demo includes training scripts, ONNX export, quantization deployment, and accuracy testing.

tour.title: Onboarding Guide
tour.description: The ONBOARD.md file provides a practical getting-started guide with usage examples, architecture overview, and step-by-step instructions for running quantization on your own models. It is the best starting point after reading this tour.
